NASB.1: 'I have made a covenant with my eyes; How then could I gaze at a virgin?
NASB.2: 'And what is the portion of God from above Or the heritage of the Almighty from on high?
NASB.3: 'Is it not calamity to the unjust And disaster to those who work iniquity?
NASB.4: 'Does He not see my ways And number all my steps?
NASB.5: 'If I have walked with falsehood, And my foot has hastened after deceit,
NASB.6: Let Him weigh me with accurate scales, And let God know my integrity.
NASB.7: 'If my step has turned from the way, Or my heart followed my eyes, Or if any spot has stuck to my hands,
NASB.8: Let me sow and another eat, And let my crops be uprooted.
NASB.9: 'If my heart has been enticed by a woman, Or I have lurked at my neighbor's doorway,
NASB.10: May my wife grind for another, And let others kneel down over her.
NASB.11: 'For that would be a lustful crime; Moreover, it would be an iniquity [punishable by] judges.
NASB.12: 'For it would be fire that consumes to Abaddon, And would uproot all my increase.
NASB.13: 'If I have despised the claim of my male or female slaves When they filed a complaint against me,
NASB.14: What then could I do when God arises? And when He calls me to account, what will I answer Him?
NASB.15: 'Did not He who made me in the womb make him, And the same one fashion us in the womb?
NASB.16: 'If I have kept the poor from [their] desire, Or have caused the eyes of the widow to fail,
NASB.17: Or have eaten my morsel alone, And the orphan has not shared it
NASB.18: (But from my youth he grew up with me as with a father, And from infancy I guided her),
NASB.19: If I have seen anyone perish for lack of clothing, Or that the needy had no covering,
NASB.20: If his loins have not thanked me, And if he has not been warmed with the fleece of my sheep,
NASB.21: If I have lifted up my hand against the orphan, Because I saw I had support in the gate,
NASB.22: Let my shoulder fall from the socket, And my arm be broken off at the elbow.
NASB.23: 'For calamity from God is a terror to me, And because of His majesty I can do nothing.
NASB.24: 'If I have put my confidence [in] gold, And called fine gold my trust,
NASB.25: If I have gloated because my wealth was great, And because my hand had secured [so] much;
NASB.26: If I have looked at the sun when it shone Or the moon going in splendor,
NASB.27: And my heart became secretly enticed, And my hand threw a kiss from my mouth,
NASB.28: That too would have been an iniquity [calling for] judgment, For I would have denied God above.
NASB.29: 'Have I rejoiced at the extinction of my enemy, Or exulted when evil befell him?
NASB.30: 'No, I have not allowed my mouth to sin By asking for his life in a curse.
NASB.31: 'Have the men of my tent not said, 'Who can find one who has not been satisfied with his meat '?
NASB.32: 'The alien has not lodged outside, [For] I have opened my doors to the traveler.
NASB.33: 'Have I covered my transgressions like Adam, By hiding my iniquity in my bosom,
NASB.34: Because I feared the great multitude, And the contempt of families terrified me, And kept silent and did not go out of doors?
NASB.35: 'Oh that I had one to hear me! Behold, here is my signature; Let the Almighty answer me! And the indictment which my adversary has written,
NASB.36: Surely I would carry it on my shoulder, I would bind it to myself like a crown.
NASB.37: 'I would declare to Him the number of my steps; Like a prince I would approach Him.
NASB.38: 'If my land cries out against me, And its furrows weep together;
NASB.39: If I have eaten its fruit without money, Or have caused its owners to lose their lives,
NASB.40: Let briars grow instead of wheat, And stinkweed instead of barley.' The words of Job are ended.

ESV.1: “I have made a covenant with my eyes; how then could I gaze at a virgin?
ESV.2: What would be my portion from God above and my heritage from the Almighty on high?
ESV.3: Is not calamity for the unrighteous, and disaster for the workers of iniquity?
ESV.4: Does not he see my ways and number all my steps?
ESV.5: “If I have walked with falsehood and my foot has hastened to deceit;
ESV.6: (Let me be weighed in a just balance, and let God know my integrity!)
ESV.7: if my step has turned aside from the way and my heart has gone after my eyes, and if any spot has stuck to my hands,
ESV.8: then let me sow, and another eat, and let what grows for me  be rooted out.
ESV.9: “If my heart has been enticed toward a woman, and I have lain in wait at my neighbor's door,
ESV.10: then let my wife grind for another, and let others bow down on her.
ESV.11: For that would be a heinous crime; that would be an iniquity to be punished by the judges;
ESV.12: for that would be a fire that consumes as far as Abaddon, and it would burn to the root all my increase.
ESV.13: “If I have rejected the cause of my manservant or my maidservant, when they brought a complaint against me,
ESV.14: what then shall I do when God rises up? When he makes inquiry, what shall I answer him?
ESV.15: Did not he who made me in the womb make him? And did not one fashion us in the womb?
ESV.16: “If I have withheld anything that the poor desired, or have caused the eyes of the widow to fail,
ESV.17: or have eaten my morsel alone, and the fatherless has not eaten of it
ESV.18: (for from my youth the fatherless  grew up with me as with a father, and from my mother's womb I guided the widow ),
ESV.19: if I have seen anyone perish for lack of clothing, or the needy without covering,
ESV.20: if his body has not blessed me,  and if he was not warmed with the fleece of my sheep,
ESV.21: if I have raised my hand against the fatherless, because I saw my help in the gate,
ESV.22: then let my shoulder blade fall from my shoulder, and let my arm be broken from its socket.
ESV.23: For I was in terror of calamity from God, and I could not have faced his majesty.
ESV.24: “If I have made gold my trust or called fine gold my confidence,
ESV.25: if I have rejoiced because my wealth was abundant or because my hand had found much,
ESV.26: if I have looked at the sun  when it shone, or the moon moving in splendor,
ESV.27: and my heart has been secretly enticed, and my mouth has kissed my hand,
ESV.28: this also would be an iniquity to be punished by the judges, for I would have been false to God above.
ESV.29: “If I have rejoiced at the ruin of him who hated me, or exulted when evil overtook him
ESV.30: (I have not let my mouth sin by asking for his life with a curse),
ESV.31: if the men of my tent have not said, ‘Who is there that has not been filled with his meat?’
ESV.32: (the sojourner has not lodged in the street; I have opened my doors to the traveler),
ESV.33: if I have concealed my transgressions as others do  by hiding my iniquity in my heart,
ESV.34: because I stood in great fear of the multitude, and the contempt of families terrified me, so that I kept silence, and did not go out of doors —
ESV.35: Oh, that I had one to hear me! (Here is my signature! Let the Almighty answer me!) Oh, that I had the indictment written by my adversary!
ESV.36: Surely I would carry it on my shoulder; I would bind it on me as a crown;
ESV.37: I would give him an account of all my steps; like a prince I would approach him.
ESV.38: “If my land has cried out against me and its furrows have wept together,
ESV.39: if I have eaten its yield without payment and made its owners breathe their last,
ESV.40: let thorns grow instead of wheat, and foul weeds instead of barley.”  The words of Job are ended.

NKJV.1: “I have made a covenant with my eyes; Why then should I look upon a young woman?
NKJV.2: For what is the allotment of God from above, And the inheritance of the Almighty from on high?
NKJV.3: Is it not destruction for the wicked, And disaster for the workers of iniquity?
NKJV.4: Does He not see my ways, And count all my steps?
NKJV.5: “If I have walked with falsehood, Or if my foot has hastened to deceit,
NKJV.6: Let me be weighed on honest scales, That God may know my integrity.
NKJV.7: If my step has turned from the way, Or my heart walked after my eyes, Or if any spot adheres to my hands,
NKJV.8: Then let me sow, and another eat; Yes, let my harvest be rooted out.
NKJV.9: “If my heart has been enticed by a woman, Or if I have lurked at my neighbor’s door,
NKJV.10: Then let my wife grind for another, And let others bow down over her.
NKJV.11: For that would be wickedness; Yes, it would be iniquity deserving of judgment.
NKJV.12: For that would be a fire that consumes to destruction, And would root out all my increase.
NKJV.13: “If I have despised the cause of my male or female servant When they complained against me,
NKJV.14: What then shall I do when God rises up? When He punishes, how shall I answer Him?
NKJV.15: Did not He who made me in the womb make them? Did not the same One fashion us in the womb?
NKJV.16: “If I have kept the poor from their desire, Or caused the eyes of the widow to fail,
NKJV.17: Or eaten my morsel by myself, So that the fatherless could not eat of it
NKJV.18: (But from my youth I reared him as a father, And from my mother’s womb I guided the widow);
NKJV.19: If I have seen anyone perish for lack of clothing, Or any poor man without covering;
NKJV.20: If his heart has not blessed me, And if he was not warmed with the fleece of my sheep;
NKJV.21: If I have raised my hand against the fatherless, When I saw I had help in the gate;
NKJV.22: Then let my arm fall from my shoulder, Let my arm be torn from the socket.
NKJV.23: For destruction from God is a terror to me, And because of His magnificence I cannot endure.
NKJV.24: “If I have made gold my hope, Or said to fine gold, ‘You are my confidence’;
NKJV.25: If I have rejoiced because my wealth was great, And because my hand had gained much;
NKJV.26: If I have observed the sun when it shines, Or the moon moving in brightness,
NKJV.27: So that my heart has been secretly enticed, And my mouth has kissed my hand;
NKJV.28: This also would be an iniquity deserving of judgment, For I would have denied God who is above.
NKJV.29: “If  I have rejoiced at the destruction of him who hated me, Or lifted myself up when evil found him
NKJV.30: (Indeed I have not allowed my mouth to sin By asking for a curse on his soul);
NKJV.31: If the men of my tent have not said, ‘Who is there that has not been satisfied with his meat?’
NKJV.32: (But no sojourner had to lodge in the street, For I have opened my doors to the traveler);
NKJV.33: If I have covered my transgressions as Adam, By hiding my iniquity in my bosom,
NKJV.34: Because I feared the great multitude, And dreaded the contempt of families, So that I kept silence And did not go out of the door—
NKJV.35: Oh, that I had one to hear me! Here is my mark. Oh, that the Almighty would answer me, That my Prosecutor had written a book!
NKJV.36: Surely I would carry it on my shoulder, And bind it on me like a crown;
NKJV.37: I would declare to Him the number of my steps; Like a prince I would approach Him.
NKJV.38: “If my land cries out against me, And its furrows weep together;
NKJV.39: If I have eaten its fruit without money, Or caused its owners to lose their lives;
NKJV.40: Then let thistles grow instead of wheat, And weeds instead of barley.” The words of Job are ended.

NLT.1:
“I made a covenant with my eyes
not to look with lust at a young woman.
NLT.2:
For what has God above chosen for us?
What is our inheritance from the Almighty on high?
NLT.3:
Isn’t it calamity for the wicked
and misfortune for those who do evil?
NLT.4:
Doesn’t he see everything I do
and every step I take?
NLT.5:
“Have I lied to anyone
or deceived anyone?
NLT.6:
Let God weigh me on the scales of justice,
for he knows my integrity.
NLT.7:
If I have strayed from his pathway,
or if my heart has lusted for what my eyes have seen,
or if I am guilty of any other sin,
NLT.8:
then let someone else eat the crops I have planted.
Let all that I have planted be uprooted.
NLT.9:
“If my heart has been seduced by a woman,
or if I have lusted for my neighbor’s wife,
NLT.10:
then let my wife serve another man;
let other men sleep with her.
NLT.11:
For lust is a shameful sin,
a crime that should be punished.
NLT.12:
It is a fire that burns all the way to hell.
It would wipe out everything I own.
NLT.13:
“If I have been unfair to my male or female servants
when they brought their complaints to me,
NLT.14:
how could I face God?
What could I say when he questioned me?
NLT.15:
For God created both me and my servants.
He created us both in the womb.
NLT.16:
“Have I refused to help the poor,
or crushed the hopes of widows?
NLT.17:
Have I been stingy with my food
and refused to share it with orphans?
NLT.18:
No, from childhood I have cared for orphans like a father,
and all my life I have cared for widows.
NLT.19:
Whenever I saw the homeless without clothes
and the needy with nothing to wear,
NLT.20:
did they not praise me
for providing wool clothing to keep them warm?
NLT.21:
“If I raised my hand against an orphan,
knowing the judges would take my side,
NLT.22:
then let my shoulder be wrenched out of place!
Let my arm be torn from its socket!
NLT.23:
That would be better than facing God’s judgment.
For if the majesty of God opposes me, what hope is there?
NLT.24:
“Have I put my trust in money
or felt secure because of my gold?
NLT.25:
Have I gloated about my wealth
and all that I own?
NLT.26:
“Have I looked at the sun shining in the skies,
or the moon walking down its silver pathway,
NLT.27:
and been secretly enticed in my heart
to throw kisses at them in worship?
NLT.28:
If so, I should be punished by the judges,
for it would mean I had denied the God of heaven.
NLT.29:
“Have I ever rejoiced when disaster struck my enemies,
or become excited when harm came their way?
NLT.30:
No, I have never sinned by cursing anyone
or by asking for revenge.
NLT.31:
“My servants have never said,
‘He let others go hungry.’
NLT.32:
I have never turned away a stranger
but have opened my doors to everyone.
NLT.33:
“Have I tried to hide my sins like other people do,
concealing my guilt in my heart?
NLT.34:
Have I feared the crowd
or the contempt of the masses,
so that I kept quiet and stayed indoors?
NLT.35:
“If only someone would listen to me!
Look, I will sign my name to my defense.
Let the Almighty answer me.
Let my accuser write out the charges against me.
NLT.36:
I would face the accusation proudly.
I would wear it like a crown.
NLT.37:
For I would tell him exactly what I have done.
I would come before him like a prince.
NLT.38:
“If my land accuses me
and all its furrows cry out together,
NLT.39:
or if I have stolen its crops
or murdered its owners,
NLT.40:
then let thistles grow on that land instead of wheat,
and weeds instead of barley.”
Job’s words are ended.

AMP.1:
"I have made a covenant (agreement) with my eyes;
How then could I gaze [lustfully] at a virgin?
AMP.2:
"For what is the portion I would have from God above,
And what heritage from the Almighty on high?
AMP.3:
"Does not tragedy fall [justly] on the unjust
And disaster to those who work wickedness?
AMP.4:
"Does not God see my ways
And count all my steps?
AMP.5:
"If I have walked with falsehood,
Or if my foot has chased after deceit,
AMP.6:
Oh, let Him weigh me with accurate scales,
And let God know my integrity.
AMP.7:
"If my step has turned away from the way [of God],
Or if my heart has [covetously] followed my eyes,
Or if any spot [of guilt] has stained my hands,
AMP.8:
Then let me plant and [let] another eat [from the results of my labor],
And let my crops be uprooted and ruined.
AMP.9:
"If my heart has been enticed and I was made a fool by a woman,
Or if I have [covetously] lurked at my neighbor's door [until his departure],
AMP.10:
Let my wife grind [meal, like a bond slave] for another [man],
And let others kneel down over her.
AMP.11:
"For adultery is a heinous and lustful crime;
Moreover, it would be a sin punishable by the judges.
AMP.12:
"For it is a fire which consumes to Abaddon (destruction, ruin, final torment);
And [illicit passion] would burn and rage and uproot all my [life's] increase [destroying everything].
AMP.13:
"If I have despised and rejected the claim of my male or female servants
When they filed a complaint against me,
AMP.14:
What then could I do when God arises [to judge me]?
When He calls me to account, what will I answer Him?
AMP.15:
"Did not He who made me in the womb make my servant,
And did not the same One fashion us both in the womb?
AMP.16:
"If I have withheld from the poor what they desired,
Or have caused the eyes of the widow to look in vain [for relief],
AMP.17:
Or have eaten my morsel [of food] alone,
And did not share it with the orphan
AMP.18:
(But from my youth the orphan grew up with me as with a father,
And from my mother's womb I have been the widow's guide),
AMP.19:
If I have seen anyone perish for lack of clothing,
Or any poor person without covering,
AMP.20:
If his loins have not thanked and blessed me [for clothing them],
And if he was not warmed with the fleece of my sheep,
AMP.21:
If I have lifted my hand against the orphan,
Because I saw [that the judges would be] my help at the [council] gate,
AMP.22:
Then let my shoulder fall away from its socket,
And my arm be broken off at the elbow.
AMP.23:
"For tragedy from God is a terror to me,
And because of His majesty and exaltation I can do nothing [nor endure facing Him].
AMP.24:
"If I have put my trust and confidence in gold,
Or have declared fine gold my hope and assurance,
AMP.25:
If I gloated and rejoiced because my wealth was great,
And because my [powerful] hand [alone] had obtained so much,
AMP.26:
If I beheld the sun [as an object of worship] when it shone
Or the moon going in its splendor,
AMP.27:
And my heart became secretly enticed [by them],
And my hand threw a kiss from my mouth [in respect to them],
AMP.28:
This also would have been [a heinous] sin calling for judgment,
For I would have denied God above.
AMP.29:
"Have I rejoiced at the destruction of the enemy [who hated me],
Or exulted [in malicious triumph] when evil overtook him?
AMP.30:
"No, I have not allowed my mouth to sin
By cursing my enemy and asking for his life.
AMP.31:
"I assure you, the men of my tent have said,
'Who can find one [in need] who has not been satisfied with his meat'?
AMP.32:
"The stranger has not lodged in the street,
Because I have opened my door to the traveler.
AMP.33:
"Have I concealed my transgressions like Adam or like other men,
By hiding my wickedness in my bosom,
AMP.34:
Because I feared the great multitude,
And the contempt of families terrified me,
So that I kept silence and did not acknowledge my sin and did not go out of the door?
AMP.35:
"Oh, that I had one to listen to me!
Look, here is my signature (mark);
Let the Almighty answer me!
Let my adversary write out His indictment [and put His vague accusations in tangible form].
AMP.36:
"Surely I would [proudly] bear it on my shoulder,
And bind the scroll around my head like a crown.
AMP.37:
"I would count out to Him the number of my steps [with every detail of my life],
Approaching His presence as if I were a prince.
AMP.38:
"For if my land has cried out against me,
And its furrows weep together;
AMP.39:
If I have eaten its fruits without paying for them,
Or have caused its [rightful] owners to lose their lives,
AMP.40:
Let thorns grow instead of wheat,
And stinkweed and cockleburs instead of barley."
So the words of Job [with his friends] are finished.

or gloated over the trouble that came to him—
NIV.30:
I have not allowed my mouth to sin
by invoking a curse against his life—
NIV.31:
if the men of my household have never said,
‘Who has not had his fill of Job’s meat?’—
NIV.32:
but no stranger had to spend the night in the street,
for my door was always open to the traveler—
NIV.33:
if I have concealed my sin as men do,
by hiding my guilt in my heart
NIV.34:
because I so feared the crowd
and so dreaded the contempt of the clans
that I kept silent and would not go outside—
NIV.35:
(“Oh, that I had someone to hear me!
I sign now my defense—let the Almighty answer me;
let my accuser put his indictment in writing.
NIV.36:
Surely I would wear it on my shoulder,
I would put it on like a crown.
NIV.37:
I would give him an account of my every step;
like a prince I would approach him.)—
NIV.38:
“if my land cries out against me
and all its furrows are wet with tears,
NIV.39:
if I have devoured its yield without payment
or broken the spirit of its tenants,
NIV.40:
then let briers come up instead of wheat
and weeds instead of barley.”
The words of Job are ended.
